This is why Microsoft's purchase of Xamarin is huge for the future of Windows 10

That means a small team of 4 developers working on Android and iOS would pay the prices here 8 times once a year – a little under $8000. An Indie would be looking at around $600 per year for both platforms but crucially wouldn't get the fantastic Visual Studio integration, which would cost £2000 per year.

This project is dead in the water. And why on earth would an iOS app developer crate an app that could run on an Windows phone but no one has a Windows phone? Instead if wasting energy and resources in making that app compatible you better spend that time and energy to only make it on iOS. Simpler code, no fuzzing around with compatibility issues, simpler to design since you only need one IOS device to test on, and better to develop because all you need to do is know iOS best and not worry about Windows compatibility.

In any application design, making your lower code compatible for 2 systems makes the code much more complex, harder to debug and less performant.
